shortDescription: European forward power prices extended gains on Thursday, tracking higher gas and carbon markets, while day-ahead contracts in Germany and France edged up on lower renewable output.

children: European forward power prices extended gains on Thursday, tracking higher gas and carbon markets, while day-ahead contracts in Germany and France edged up on lower renewable output.
The German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) rose 1.5% to €130.7 per megawatt-hour at 0835 GMT, a high since October 2023, LSEG data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) rose 1.7% to €88/MWh, a high since May 2024, according to LSEG data.
Higher month-ahead gas prices are the main driver, reinforced by firmer carbon and low gas storage levels before winter, EnergyScan analysts said.
"While the biggest increase is concentrated at the front of the curve, further calendar maturities are also experiencing the increase as risk rolls along the curve," they said.
United States President Donald Trump said he expected the war with Iran to end after the November U.S. midterm elections while both sides continued to attack ships near the Strait of Hormuz.

Front-month and front-quarter contracts continued to rise on the news, with the French winter quarter contracts rising over €150/MWh and the German contracts over €170/MWh, LSEG data showed. (0#TRFRBc) (0#TRDEBc)
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was up 0.4% to €85.91 a metric ton.
On the spot side, contracts edged higher as renewable supply was seen dropping in Germany and France.
The German day-ahead ticked up 0.6% to €196.50/MWh while the French equivalent added 2.4% to €178/MWh, LSEG data showed. (TRDEBD1) (TRFRBD1)
German wind power supply is forecast to fall by 3.2 GW to 7.9 GW on Tuesday, while solar was seen down 800 megawatts, the data showed.
French wind and solar supply was expected to drop by 200 MW each, the data showed.
French nuclear availability fell by two percentage points to 74% of total capacity as a reactor went offline with a planned outage.
